# Context

This script provides select code to identify dual eligible enrollees with same-insurer status. The code assumes the user has created a table called "mbsf" with one row per beneficiary-month-Medicaid plan. An individual with one Medicaid plan will have one row per month observed, an individual with two Medicaid plans (e.g. an MCO plan and a stand alone MLTSS plan) will have two rows for each month observed, one row where the Medicaid plan is the MCO and a second row where the Medicaid plan is the MLTSS plan. The table should include the following variables:  

- bene_id  
- death date  
- state  
- year  
- month  
- MA contract id  
- MA plan id  
- MA parent organization (from the Plan Characteristics File Base segment)  
- TAF managed care plan id  
- TAF parent organization (from the CHSE Managed Care Crosswalk)  

This script provides code to load and clean Medicare and Medicaid parent organization names in order to flag names that match (i.e. same_insurer_status == 1). Once matches have been identified, users can merge the same_insurer_flag to their mbsf table by medicare parent organization, medicaid parent organization, state, and year. Finally, we provide code to categorize same-insurer status so that the mbsf table can be aggregated to beneficiary-month level. 


# Required Packages 

```{r}
library(data.table)
library(magrittr) 
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(readxl)
```


# Identify MA parent orgs

This chunk of code loads Medicare parent organizations from the Plan Characteristics File Base segment, merges them to their service state from the Plan Characteristics Service Area segment, and cleans some parent org names to facilitate matching to Medicaid parent org names in subsequent steps.  


## Set years

```{r}
years <- c(2018, 2019, 2020, 2021)  
```


## Load Plan Characteristic File 

```{r}
# create empty table to bind to
plan_char <- data.table()

# load plan characteristics file for each year
for (year in years) {
  
  # load table
  temp <- as.data.table(readRDS(file.path(plan_char_path, paste0("plan_char_", year, ".RDS")))) 
  
  # add year
  temp[, year:= year]
  
  # bind
  plan_char <- rbind(plan_char, temp)
  
}
```


## Load Service Area File

```{r}
# create empty table to bind to
service_area <- data.table()

# load plan characteristics file for each year
for (year in years) {
  
  temp <- as.data.table(readRDS(file.path(plan_char_path, paste0("service_area_", year, ".RDS"))))
  temp[, year:= year]
  
  # bind
  service_area <- rbind(service_area, temp, fill = T)
  
  rm(temp)
}
```

# Identify TAF parent orgs
  
The mco_crosswalk variable `chse_parent_firm` represents the Medicaid parent organization. Methodologic detail is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/chse-ohsu/taf.functions/tree/main/Managed_Care_Crosswalks).  

```{r}
ma_crosswalk <- fread("mco_crosswalk_clean_20260306.csv",
                      na.strings = c("","NA","NaN"),
                      select = c("year", "state_cd", "cms_program_name", "taf_mc_plan_type_cd", "chse_parent_firm", 
                                 "cms_parent_organization", "cms_plan_name", "taf_mc_plan_name", "taf_mc_plan_id"))
```


# Match MA/TAF parent orgs

This chunk of code further cleans MA and TAF parent org names and flags those that are a match. You can then merge the match flag to your dataset by state, year, orig_medicare_parent_org, and medicaid_parent_org to identify individuals with MA and TAF plans that are owned by the same parent organization. 

```{r}
# function to further clean parent or names for matching
clean_org_name <- function(name) {
  name %>%
    str_replace_all("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1 \\2") %>%  # Add space before uppercase letter in the middle of the word
    tolower() %>% # Lowercase string
    str_replace_all("[,\\.]", "") %>%  # Remove commas
    str_replace_all("[&']", "") %>%  # Remove ampersands and apostrophes
    str_replace_all("@", "") %>%  # Remove @ symbol
    str_replace_all("\\(.*?\\)", "") %>%  # Remove anything inside parentheses
    str_replace_all("\\b(inc|corporation|llc|lp|corp|co|company|group|holding|holdings|services|system|health|healthcare|medical|the|systems|connection|county|human|at|new york|rest|realty|state|solutions|older|citizens|national|altoona|greensburg|lehigh valley|york|washington|lifeways|association)\\b", "") %>%  # Remove specified words
    trimws() %>% #Trim leading and trailing spaces
    str_replace_all("\\s", "") #delete all spaces between words
}

# clean and organize unique parent orgs
medicare_orgs <- medicare_orgs %>%
  select(parent_organization, state_cd, hardcode_parent_org, year) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(state_cd, parent_organization) %>%
  mutate(clean_name = clean_org_name(hardcode_parent_org))

medicaid_orgs <- ma_crosswalk %>%
  select(state_cd, chse_parent_firm, year) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(state_cd, chse_parent_firm) %>%
  mutate(clean_name = clean_org_name(chse_parent_firm))

# inner join medicare and medicaid orgs to get matches
matches <- merge(medicare_orgs[, .(clean_name, state_cd, year, orig_medicare_parent_org = parent_organization)], 
                      medicaid_orgs[, .(clean_name, state_cd, year, medicaid_parent_org = chse_parent_firm)], 
                      by = c("clean_name", "state_cd", "year"), 
                      all = FALSE)

# add match flag equal 1 to all rows
matches[, same_insurer_flag := 1]

# same_insurer_flag can now be merged to the user's mbsf table by state, year, medicare_parent_org, and medicaid_parent_org
```


# Create same-insurer indicators

In this section of code, we use the terms same-insurer synonymously with aligned/alignment.  

A beneficiary's Medicare and Medicaid plans are aligned if they are both owned by the same parent organization. Each beneficiary has one MA plan but may have more than one Medicaid plan. The following code creates three alignment flags:  

  1) *aligned_mco* = MCO plan (Comprehensive MCO) is aligned with MA plan *or* MCO plan includes MLTSS (Comprehensive MCO + MLTSS) and is aligned with MA plan  
  
  2) *aligned_bh* = Standalone BHO plan (Behavioral Health Organization) is aligned with MA plan *or* MCO is aligned with MA plan and person has no separate BHO*  
  
  3) *aligned_ltss* = Standalone MLTSS (MLTSS only) is aligned with MA plan *or* MCO plan includes MLTSS (Comprehensive MCO + MLTSS) and is aligned with MA plan and person has no separate MLTSS   

* In this case we assume MCO includes BH services 

At this stage of data management, prior to creating same-insurer indicators, we have a dataset called "mbsf" with one row per beneficiary-month-Medicaid plan. An individual with one Medicaid plan will have one row per month observed, an individual with two Medicaid plans (e.g. an MCO plan and a stand alone MLTSS plan) will have two rows for each month observed, one row where the Medicaid plan is the MCO and a second row where the Medicaid plan is the MLTSS plan. We have merged the "match" flag to the dataset, so rows where the Medicare and Medicaid parent are the same have match value of 1.

```{r}
# create mco alignment flag at the row level
mbsf[, aligned_mco_row := as.numeric(same_insurer_flag == 1 &
                                     mco_plan_type %in% c("cMCO", "cMCO+MLTSS"))]

# roll alignment flag to the month level
mbsf[, aligned_mco := max(aligned_mco_row), by = bene_mo]
```
 
```{r}
# create bh alignment flags at the row level, one for aligned bho and one for any standalone bho
mbsf[, sep_aligned_bh := fcase(mco_plan_type == "BHO" & same_insurer_flag == 1, 1, default = 0)]
mbsf[, sep_bh := fcase(mco_plan_type == "BHO", 1, default = 0)]

# roll alignment flags to the month level
mbsf[, has_bho_standalone := max(sep_bh), by = bene_mo]
mbsf[, has_bho_standalone_aligned:= max(sep_aligned_bh), by = bene_mo]
mbsf[, has_bho_standalone_unaligned:= as.numeric(has_bho_standalone == 1 & has_bho_standalone_aligned == 0)]

# create final aligned BH flag
mbsf[, aligned_bh := as.numeric(has_bho_standalone_aligned == 1 | (aligned_mco == 1 & has_bho_standalone == 0))]
```

```{r}
# create standalone mltss alignment flags at the row level, one for aligned mltss and one for any standalone mltss
mbsf[, sep_aligned_mltss := fcase(mco_plan_type == "MLTSS" & same_insurer_flag == 1, 1, default = 0)] 
mbsf[, sep_mltss := fcase(mco_plan_type == "MLTSS", 1, default = 0)]

# roll standalone alignment flags to the month level
mbsf[, has_ltssstandalone := max(sep_mltss), by = bene_mo]
mbsf[, has_ltssstandalone_aligned:= max(sep_aligned_mltss), by = bene_mo]
mbsf[, has_ltssstandalone_unaligned:= as.numeric(has_ltssstandalone == 1 & has_ltssstandalone_aligned == 0)]

# create MCO+MLTSS alignment flags at the row level and then roll to month level
mbsf[, aligned_mco_ltss_row := as.numeric(mco_plan_type %in% "cMCO+MLTSS" & same_insurer_flag == 1)] %>%
  .[ , aligned_mco_ltss := max(aligned_mco_ltss_row), by = bene_mo]

# create final flag for aligned MLTSS
mbsf[, aligned_ltss := as.numeric(has_ltssstandalone_aligned == 1 | 
                                  (aligned_mco_ltss == 1 & has_ltssstandalone == 0))]

# create final alignment category at the bene-month level
mbsf[, align_cat := fcase(
  aligned_mco == 0 & aligned_bh == 0 & aligned_ltss == 0, "Not aligned",
  aligned_mco == 1 & aligned_bh == 1 & aligned_ltss == 1, "Aligned with MCO + MLTSS + BHO",
  aligned_mco == 1 & aligned_bh == 0 & aligned_ltss == 1, "Aligned with MCO + MLTSS",
  aligned_mco == 0 & aligned_bh == 1 & aligned_ltss == 0, "Aligned with BHO",
  aligned_mco == 0 & aligned_bh == 0 & aligned_ltss == 1, "Aligned with MLTSS",
  aligned_mco == 1 & aligned_bh == 1 & aligned_ltss == 0, "Aligned with MCO + BHO",
  aligned_mco == 1 & aligned_bh == 0 & aligned_ltss == 0, "Aligned with MCO",
  aligned_mco == 0 & aligned_bh == 1 & aligned_ltss == 1, "Aligned with MLTSS + BHO",
  default = NA_character_
)]

# data can now be aggregated to the beneficiary month level
# keep only nec. vars that are the same across bene_mos
keep_cols <- c("bene_id", "year", "calendar_mo", "study_mo", "state_res",
               "age", "age_cat", "sex", "rti_race_cd", "bene_dob", "death_dt",
               "orec", 
               "ptc_cntrct_id_cd", "ptc_pbp_id_cd", "contract_name", "plan_name", 
               "plan_type", "medicare_parent_organization",
               "snp_type", "fide_snp",
               "bene_mo", "person_mo_id", "state_fips_cd", "cnty_fips_cd",
               "aligned_mco", "aligned_bh", "aligned_ltss", 
               "has_bho_standalone_aligned", "has_bho_standalone_unaligned",  
               "has_ltssstandalone_aligned", "has_ltssstandalone_unaligned",
               "aligned_mco_ltss", "align_cat")

# keep nec. cols
mbsf <- mbsf[, ..keep_cols]

# roll up to bene_mo
mbsf <- unique(mbsf)
```


# Identify MA plan type

We use two sources to identify the ma_plan_type as "standard_ma", "fide", "hide", or "co" (coordination only):  
  - [Medicare Plan Characteristics File](https://resdac.org/cms-data/files/plan-characteristics)
  - [SMAC D-SNP Integration Status reports](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/medicaid-coordination/about/dsnps)   

The MA plan characteristics file includes the following variables:  
  * snp_type  
    - 0 (not an SNP)  
    - C (chronic/disabling condition)  
    - D (dual elig)  
    - I (institutional)  
  * fide_snp  
    - Y (yes)  
    - N (no)  
    - 9 (not applicable)    

The Integration Status report includes:  
  * integration_status
    - HIDE
    - FIDE
    - Coordination-Only  

```{r}
# create contract_plan_id in mbsf
mbsf[, contract_plan_id := paste0(ptc_cntrct_id_cd, ptc_pbp_id_cd)]

# merge snp_type and fide_snp from plan characteristics file to the mbsf table
# create standard MA vs SNP 
mbsf[, standard_ma:= fcase(snp_type %in% c('C', 'D', 'I'), 'snp', default = 'standard_ma')]

# create fide: yes/no
mbsf[, fide := fcase(fide_snp == "Y", 1, default = 0)]

# load CMS AIP report
aip <- data.table(read_excel("SMACDSNPIntegrationStatusesDataCY2021.xlsx",
                  sheet = "CY2021 Data",
                  skip = 1) %>% janitor::clean_names()) 

# Note: R1548 offers one PBP in VA and NC. Because it is an RPPO, the integration status at the contract level is marked as the lowest level of integration, coordination-only; however, the VA SMAC on its own does meet HIDE status. We will update this below

# check R1548
aip[grepl("R1548", contract_number), .(contract_number, plan_id, state, integration_status)]

# remove * from contract_number
aip[, contract_number := gsub("\\*", "", contract_number)]

# concatenate contract_id and plan_id
aip[, contract_plan_id := paste0(contract_number, plan_id)]

# temporarily change VA integration status to match R1548001 in NC
aip[state=="VA" & contract_plan_id == "R1548001", integration_status:=  "Coordination-Only"]

# merge
mbsf <- merge(mbsf,
              unique(aip[, .(contract_plan_id, integration_status,
                             aip = applicable_integrated_plan)]),
              by = c("contract_plan_id"),
              all.x = T)

# change VA integration status back to HIDE
mbsf[state_res=="VA" & contract_plan_id == "R1548001", integration_status:=  "HIDE"]

# create final ma_plan_type
mbsf[, ma_plan_type:= fcase(standard_ma=="standard_ma", "standard_ma",
                            integration_status == "FIDE", "fide",
                            integration_status == "HIDE", "hide",
                            integration_status == "Coordination-Only", "co",
                            default = NA_character_)]
```
